Some notes from me (Ines)

Pictures I have:
- about 60 photos of dishes and the jar wall, taken by Priya Nair for the
  restaurant's website
- my own phone photos of the larder, labels and all
- scans of all four issues of Brine (drawings by my friend Olu)
- a photo of my grandmother's ogiri pot

Things people ask me about: the jar wall, the koji room (it is a cupboard),
the staff meal, and the workshops I run on the first Monday of the month.

I took over the kitchen in September 2022.

Books that got me here: The Art of Fermentation by Sandor Katz, and Wild
Fermentation. And my grandmother, who never measured anything.
(Saved from LinkedIn as text, October 2026)

Ines Okafor
Head Chef at Saltmarsh. Fermentation, whole-vegetable cooking, apprentices.
Leeds, England, United Kingdom

ABOUT
I cook at Saltmarsh, a 40-seat restaurant in Leeds. Most of what I care about
happens before service: what we do with the trim, the whey, the stems and the
bones. We have a wall of jars and a prep list that is longer than the menu.
I run our apprentice programme and write a small zine about preserving,
called Brine.

EXPERIENCE

Head Chef, Saltmarsh, Leeds
Mar 2022 to present
- A menu that changes every week
- Cut kitchen food waste from 14 kg to 5 kg a week
- Built the larder: 40+ ferments, vinegars and garums on rotation
- Two apprentices a year since 2023

Sous Chef, The Corn Exchange Kitchen, Leeds
Jun 2019 to Feb 2022
- Ran the pass on a 90-cover service
- Took over ordering and brought the supplier list from 31 to 12

Chef de Partie, Brassica, Manchester
Sep 2016 to May 2019
- Larder and garnish, then sauce

Fjaerland Fermentation Lab, Norway
Jan 2018 to Mar 2018

EDUCATION
Leeds Kitchen College. Diploma in Professional Cookery, 2014 to 2016

VOLUNTEERING
Sunday Pot, Leeds. Co-founder. 2021 to present
A hot meal every Sunday at St Aidan's hall, cooked from what restaurants in
the city have left over.

PUBLICATIONS
Brine. A zine about preserving. Four issues, 2022 to 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Callum Reyes, owner of Saltmarsh:
"Ines turned our bins into a larder. The best thing on the menu most weeks
started as something we used to throw away."

item.text:
The strongest direction is **“The Living Larder”**: a portfolio that feels like stepping into your kitchen at Saltmarsh. Fermentation gives the 3D and scroll movement a purpose—showing how ingredients change over time.

I’ve reviewed both files in `material`. They contain your background and notes about photographs and zine scans; the images themselves aren’t present. Nothing has been built.

### Visual direction

An editorial, tactile style inspired by handwritten jar labels and *Brine*: warm cream, ink black, deep green, and amber glass. Large typography, close-up food photography, and small annotations would make it feel personal and rooted in your work.

The main visual would be a **3D fermentation jar**, with light moving through the glass. As visitors scroll, it rotates slowly and introduces the story behind your larder. Photography would remain central to showing your actual cooking.

### Page plan

| Section | Content | Movement |
|---|---|---|
| **Opening** | “Ines Okafor — Chef, fermenter, keeper of the larder.” A short introduction to Saltmarsh and Leeds. | A large 3D jar turns gently as the introduction comes into view. |
| **Before service** | Your approach to trim, whey, stems, and bones. Feature the reduction in kitchen waste from **14 kg to 5 kg a week**. | A short scroll sequence follows an ingredient from preparation to preservation to plate. |
| **The jar wall** | Explore your **40+ rotating ferments, vinegars, and garums**, using selected real examples. | A layered shelf gains depth as you scroll; selecting a jar opens its story. |
| **On the plate** | A tightly edited selection of dishes, with captions connecting the plate to the larder. | Large photographs reveal with subtle shifts in position. |
| **Passed down, passed on** | Your grandmother’s ogiri pot, apprentices, monthly workshops, and Sunday Pot. | A calmer photographic section, letting the personal story take focus. |
| **Brine** | All four issues of your preserving zine, crediting Olu’s drawings. | Covers appear as dimensional paper objects; select one for readable pages or excerpts. |
| **Background & contact** | A compact career history, Callum Reyes’s recommendation, and contact links. | Minimal motion, with a clear route to get in touch. |

### How the interaction should feel

One memorable 3D centerpiece, supported by smaller movements throughout the page. Avoid making every section a spectacle: the rhythm should alternate between immersive moments and quiet reading.

Scrolling stays natural, with no forced scroll speed. Every jar and zine interaction also works through tapping and keyboard controls. Mobile gets a simpler composition; reduced-motion preferences get static imagery and straightforward transitions.

### Build approach, when authorized

Use a lightweight page framework, with Three.js for the jar and scroll-linked animation for selected sections. Load the 3D experience progressively so visitors can read immediately. Optimize photographs and provide a static fallback for devices that struggle with 3D.

### Details to resolve before building

- Select photographs and scans from the assets you described, and confirm permission and credits for their use.
- Confirm the timeline: LinkedIn lists Head Chef from March 2022; your notes say you took over the kitchen in September 2022. These may represent different milestones.
- Supply contact details, workshop links, and actual jar and dish stories for the featured examples.

The site should leave visitors remembering your cooking, resourcefulness, and teaching—with the motion helping tell those stories.
